::: {#exm-posterior-predictive}
#### Will the next mother smoke?

Let $Y^{\mathrm{new}} = 1$ if one more mother from the `birthwt` population smoked during pregnancy,
and $Y^{\mathrm{new}} = 0$ if she did not.
Given $\prob$,

$$
\Prf{Y^{\mathrm{new}} = 1 \mid \prob} = \prob.
$$

With the posterior $\p(\prob \mid \vy)$ of @exm-prior-posterior-figure,

$$
\ba
\Prf{Y^{\mathrm{new}} = 1 \mid \vy}
&= \int_0^1 \Prf{Y^{\mathrm{new}} = 1 \mid \prob}\, \p(\prob \mid \vy)\, d\prob
&& \text{(definition of the posterior predictive distribution)}\\
&= \int_0^1 \prob\, \p(\prob \mid \vy)\, d\prob
&& \text{(Bernoulli model)}\\
&= \E{\prob \mid \vy}
&& \text{(definition of the posterior mean)}.
\ea
$$

So the posterior predictive probability that the next mother smoked
is the posterior mean of $\prob$,
`r round(post_summary["real (birthwt)", "mean"], 3)`.
The code below checks this by simulation:
draw $\prob$ from its posterior,
then draw $Y^{\mathrm{new}}$ given that $\prob$.

::: {.panel-tabset group="language"}

##### R

```{r}
#| label: posterior-predictive-next
#| code-fold: false
set.seed(2)
prob_draws <- stats::rbeta(
  10000,
  post_params["real (birthwt)", "a"],
  post_params["real (birthwt)", "b"]
)
y_new <- stats::rbinom(10000, size = 1, prob = prob_draws)
c(
  simulated = mean(y_new),
  exact = post_summary["real (birthwt)", "mean"]
)
```

##### Python

```{python}
#| label: posterior-predictive-next-py
#| code-fold: false
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

smoke_y = pd.read_csv("data/birthwt.csv")["smoke"].to_numpy()
post_a = 1 + smoke_y.sum()
post_b = 1 + len(smoke_y) - smoke_y.sum()

rng = np.random.default_rng(2)
prob_draws = rng.beta(post_a, post_b, size=10000)
y_new = rng.binomial(1, prob_draws)
{"simulated": y_new.mean(), "exact": post_a / (post_a + post_b)}
```
